description: The notified Ecuadorian Technical Regulation applies to the following taps and valves for household use marketed in Ecuador, whether manufactured domestically or imported:• Automatic compensating valves for individual, wall-mounted shower systems• Bath and shower tapsG/TBT/N/ECU/180/Rev.1- 2 - • Bidet taps• Washing machine taps• Taps for drinking fountains• Shut-off valves for humidifiers• Taps for wash-basins and kitchen sinks• Laundry room taps• Garden taps• Metering and automatic shut-off valves• Shower heads, handheld showers and shower body jets• Shut-off valves up to 2.54 cm (1 inch).The notified Ecuadorian Technical Regulation does not apply to:• Drainage fittings for sanitary ware, including wastes and traps, covered by NTE INEN 2901.• Flexible connectors for water under continuous pressure, covered by ASME A112.18.6/CSA B125.6.• Automatic temperature control and pressure compensating valves or taps, covered by ASSE 1016/ASME A112.1016/CSA B125.16.• Flushometers.

title: Proyecto de Reforma Sustitutiva de la Resolución ARCSA-DE-002-2020-JCGO, a través de la cual se expide la "Normativa Técnica Sanitaria de buenas prácticas de almacenamiento, distribución y/o transporte para establecimientos farmacéuticos y establecimientos de dispositivos médicos de uso humano" (Draft substitute amendment to Resolution ARCSA-DE-002-2020-JCGO issuing the Technical Sanitary Regulations on good practices for storage, distribution and/or transportation for pharmaceutical establishments and establishments for medical devices for human use)
description: The notified draft substitute amendment to Resolution ARCSA-DE-002-2020-JCGO issuing the Technical Sanitary Regulations on good practices for storage, distribution and/or transportation for pharmaceutical establishments and establishments for medical devices for human use, is intended to establish the requirements and guidelines for granting good storage, distribution and/or transportation practices certificates to pharmaceutical establishments and medical device 1 This information can be provided by including a website address, a PDF attachment, or other information on where the text of the final/modified measure and/or interpretative guidance can be obtained.G/TBT/N/ECU/504/Add.6- 2 - establishments that store, distribute and transport medicinal products in general, medicinal gases, medicines containing controlled substances, biological products, homoeopathic products or medicines, processed natural products for medicinal use, medical devices for human use, products for the pharmaceutical industry, and active pharmaceutical ingredients; with the aim of conserving the properties and maintaining the quality, safety and effectiveness of these products.The provisions set forth in these Regulations are mandatory and apply to natural and legal persons, whether domestic or foreign, established within the national territory, who are owners or legal representatives of: distributors of medicinal gases, distributors of active pharmaceutical ingredients, pharmaceutical representative offices, distributors of pharmaceuticals, companies providing logistics and/or storage services for pharmaceutical products, representative offices and distributors of medical devices and/or in vitro diagnostic biochemical reagents for human use, medical device logistics and/or storage facilities, whether public or private, covered by the regulations on operating permits for establishments subject to health controls and surveillance; that store, distribute and/or transport the aforementioned products.Agency:Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo, MDEP (Ministry of Economic and Productive Development)Subsecretaría de Calidad (Under-Secretariat for Quality)Primary enquiry point: Andrea SegoviaPlataforma Gubernamental de Gestión FinancieraAv. Amazonas entre Unión Nacional de Periodistas y Alfonso Pereira, Piso 1, Bloque amarilloQuito EC170522Tel.: (+593) 2394 8760, Ext. 2254 or 2252Email: puntocontacto-otcecu@produccion.gob.ec; puntocontactoecu@gmail.com; aesegovia@produccion.gob.ecWebsite: http://www.produccion.gob.ec__________

title: Draft Commission Implementing Decision (EU) repealing Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2284 postponing the expiry date of the approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine for use in biocidal products of product-type 18 in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council
description:
This draft Commission Implementing Decision repeals the latest postponement of the expiry date of the approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine as an active substance for use in biocidal products of product-type (PT) 18.

On 28 July 2020, an application was submitted in accordance with Article 13(1) of the Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council (BPR) for the renewal of the approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 18. 

Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/1285 postponed the expiry date of approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 18 to 31 July 2024, and Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/787 postponed further the expiry date to 31 January 2026. Finally, the expiry date was again extended, to 31 July 2027, by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2284.

On 27 May 2026 the Agency adopted its opinion on magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 18, having regard to the conclusions of the evaluating competent authority.

Given the opinion of the Agency, it is appropriate to renew the approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 18. Consequently, a draft Implementing Regulation is being prepared to renew the approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 18 (examination procedure under Regulation (EU) No 182/2011).

Further to that Implementing Regulation, it is necessary to repeal the latest postponement of the expiry date of the approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine. The present draft Decision therefore intends to repeal Decision (EU) 2025/2284 postponing the expiry date of the approval of magnesium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 18.

Amendments to the Gaming Machine Technical Standards
description:
Following the consultation on proposed changes to the Gaming Machine Technical Standards (GMTS) and Gaming Machine Testing Strategy, the Gambling Commission has published its response on 30 September 2026. There is a staged implementation timeline of 30 March 2027, 30 June 2027 and 3 October 2028. Following consultation feedback and evidence supplied the changes to be implemented include;

 

· Definition of a session

· The classification of gaming machines and/or games as ‘new’ or ‘existing’ 

· Limit setting

· Breaks in play

· Staff alerts

title: Public Health Protection (Food) (Iodized table salt enrichment), 5786 – 2026
description:
Israeli research indicates a significant iodine deficiency among the Israeli population: approximately 60% of the child population suffers from iodine deficiency, and approximately 85% of pregnant women suffer from iodine deficiency, which may impair the normal development of the fetus. These data require structured, systematic state intervention to prevent and correct iodine deficiency through salt iodization, which is an effective, safe, and agreed-upon method implemented in over 120 countries worldwide.

These new regulations prohibit the production or sale of table salt unless an iodine compound has been added, so the iodine content must be between 25 mg and 45 mg per kilogram of salt. It also defines terms, sets labeling requirements, and establishes a mechanism for monitoring implementation.

The regulations will enter into force 12 months after publication in Israel's Official Gazette. This period is intended to allow the Israeli salt industry and importers to prepare for implementing the new requirements.

title: Proposed revision of Ministerial Ordinance on the Specifications and Standards of Feeds and Feed Additives.
description: MAFF will amend the standard for method of manufacture of feeds in general stipulated in "Ministerial Ordinance on the Specifications and Standards of Feeds and Feed Additives" (Ordinance No. 35 of 24 July 1976 of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry). With this amendment, Guanidinoacetic acid imported into Japan as a feed additive will be permitted for use at a maximum inclusion level of 0.12% in feed for pigs and all chickens except hens, thereby increasing the maximum permitted level and expanding the scope of authorized animal species.

description: Following the approval of the draft Customs (Prohibition of Imports) (Amendment) (No. xx) Order 2026, the importation of medical device goods listed in Part I of the Third Schedule of P.U.(A) 117/2023 is subject to an approval letter issued by the Medical Device Authority (MDA) as the Point of Issuance Authority (PIA) for the regulated HS Codes, except for medical devices imported for personal use. title: Reforma parcial a la normativa técnica sanitaria para la obtención de la notificación sanitaria y control de suplementos alimenticios de los establecimientos en donde se fabrican, almacenan, distribuyen, importan y comercializan (Partial reform of the Technical Health Regulations concerning the issuance of health certificates for and the control of food supplements and establishments that manufacture, store, distribute, import or market such products)
description: The Republic of Ecuador hereby submits this addendum to the notification corresponding to the partial reform of the Technical Health Regulations concerning the issuance of health certificates for and the control of food supplements and establishments that manufacture, store, distribute, import or market such products, issued by the National Agency for Health Regulation, Control and Surveillance (ARCSA), Doctor Leopoldo Izquieta Pérez, by means of Resolution No. ARCSA-DE-2026-021-DASP.1 This information can be provided by including a website address, a PDF attachment, or other information on where the text of the final/modified measure and/or interpretative guidance can be obtained.G/TBT/N/ECU/327/Add.4- 2 - The purpose of the notified Technical Health Regulations is to establish the requirements governing the issuance of sanitary certificates for food supplements. They also set out the quality and safety requirements and guidelines with regard to the manufacturing, production, formulation, and labelling of these products, as well as the relevant  advertising, control and monitoring criteria, in the establishments that manufacture, store, distribute, import or market these products.This notification provides for a period for the submission of comments, and the notified Resolution will enter into force six months after its publication in the Official Journal.Agency:Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo, MDEP (Ministry of Economic and Productive Development)Subsecretaría de Calidad (Under-Secretariat for Quality)Primary enquiry point: Andrea SegoviaPlataforma Gubernamental de Gestión FinancieraAv. Amazonas entre Unión Nacional de Periodistas y Alfonso Pereira, Piso 1, Bloque amarillo, Quito EC170522Tel.: (+593) 2394 8760, Ext. 2254 or 2252Email: puntocontacto-otcecu@produccion.gob.ec; puntocontactoecu@gmail.com; aesegovia@produccion.gob.ecWebsite: http://www.produccion.gob.ec__________

objectivesFreeText: <p><span lang="ES"></span></p><p align="left" style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:12pt;"><span lang="ES">Objeto: la presente Normativa Técnica Sanitaria tiene por objeto establecer los requisitos bajo los cuales se otorgará la Notificación Sanitaria a los Suplementos Alimenticios.</span></p><p align="left" style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:12pt;"><span lang="ES">Además, establecer los parámetros para la fabricación, elaboración, formulación, rotulado, los parámetros de calidad e inocuidad y los criterios para la publicidad, el control y vigilancia de dichos productos en los establecimientos donde se fabrican, almacenan, distribuyen, importan y comercializan los suplementos alimenticios.</span></p><p align="left" style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:12pt;"><span lang="ES">Ámbito:&nbsp;la&nbsp;presente Normativa Técnica Sanitaria es de aplicación obligatoria para las personas naturales o jurídicas, nacionales o extranjeras, responsables de la fabricación, importación, exportación, almacenamiento, distribución y comercialización de los suplementos alimenticios en todo el territorio nacional.</span></p>

title: Proyecto de Tercera Revisión del Reglamento Técnico Ecuatoriano PRTE INEN 115 (3R) “Baterías de arranque de plomo-ácido para vehículos automotores”
description: The notified Ecuadorian Technical Regulation applies to lead-acid batteries that are used in motor vehicles categorized according to Ecuadorian Technical Standard (NTE INEN) No. 2656: Vehicle classification, whether produced domestically or imported and marketed in Ecuador:• Lead-acid batteries for motor vehicles with four or more wheels corresponding to vehicle categories M: M1, M2, and M3; and N: N1, N2, and N3.G/TBT/N/ECU/404/Rev.2- 2 - • Lead-acid batteries for motor vehicles with two, three or four wheels corresponding to vehicle categories L: L2, L3, L4, L5, L6, and L7.The notified Ecuadorian Technical Regulation does not apply to:• Lead-acid batteries incorporated into new motor vehicles.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine "On Amendments to the Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine No. 118 of 12 March 2019" (concerning the Requirements for the Safety and Quality of Milk and Dairy Products)
description:
The draft Order proposes amendments to Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine of 12 March 2019 No. 118 "On Approval of the Requirements for Safety and Quality of Milk and Dairy Products", in particular with regard to:

updating the requirements for materials and articles intended to come into contact with milk and dairy products at all stages of their production and placing on the market;

clarifying the requirements for the application of the identification mark on the packaging of milk and dairy products;

establishing requirements for providing the information contained in the identification mark in accompanying documents where products are placed in transport containers or large packages and intended for further processing, primary packaging or packaging at another establishment, as well as for liquid or powdered products transported in bulk or in tanks;

allowing the same identification mark to be used for food products subject to the Requirements and food products not subject to the Requirements when they are produced at the same establishment.

The Order is also notified under the SPS Agreement.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Extension of Collection; Standard for the Flammability of Clothing Textiles, 16 CFR Part 1610; Standard for the Flammability of Vinyl Plastic Film, 16 CFR Part 1611
description:
As required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC or Commission) announces that the Commission has submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) a request for extension of approval of information collection requirements associated with the Standard for the Flammability of Clothing Textiles and the Standard for the Flammability of Vinyl Plastic Film. OMB previously approved the collection of information under control number 3041-0024. OMB's most recent extension of approval will expire on 31 October 2026. On 25 June 2026, CPSC published a notice (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/242/Rev.1/Add.3) in the Federal Register to announce the agency's intention to seek extension of approval of the collection of information. The Commission did not receive any public comments. By publication of this notice, the Commission announces that CPSC has submitted to OMB a request for extension of approval of that collection of information.

 

Submit comments on the collection of information by 28 October 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 61209, 28 September 2026:

https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-28/pdf/2026-19748.pdf

 

This action is identified by Docket Number CPSC-2009-0092. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/CPSC-2009-0092/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 24 August 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with the CPSC and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

 

Previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/242 are identified by Docket Numbers CPSC-2009-0092 and CPSC-2019-0008.

title: Hazardous Materials: Incorporation of ASME Code Section XII and the National Board Inspection Code
description:
The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) is amending the Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) to incorporate by reference and authorize the use of the 2015 edition of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section XII--Rules for Construction and Continued Service of Transport Tanks for the construction and continued service of certain specification cargo tank motor vehicles (CTMVs), cryogenic portable tanks, and multi-unit tank car tanks. PHMSA is also amending the HMR to incorporate by reference and authorize the use of the 2015 edition of the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors National Board Inspection Code, Parts 2 and 3 (including Supplement 6) as it applies to the continued service of transport packagings constructed to ASME Section XII standards, as well as for existing CTMVs constructed in accordance with ASME requirements and the HMR. PHMSA finds these updates will result in cost savings and increased regulatory flexibility without compromising safety.

 

Effective date: 28 October 2026.    

Voluntary compliance date: 28 September 2026.    

Incorporation by reference date: The incorporation by reference of the publications listed in this rule is approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 28 October 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 61144, 28 September 2026; Title 49 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Parts 107, 171, 173, 178, 179, and 180:

title: Draft Circular promulgating QCVN 03:2026/BCT on equipment, auxiliaries and means for blending, storing and transportation of ethanol, ethanol blended gasoline - gasohol E10 at distribution terminals
description: This draft Circular promulgates QCVN 03:2026/BCT, establishing technical requirements applicable to equipment, auxiliaries and means used for blending, storing and transportation of ethanol and ethanol blended gasoline gasohol E10 at distribution terminals. The Regulation provides requirements relating to: (i) Materials compatible with fuel ethanol and Gasohol E10; (ii) Storage tanks, seals and breathing valves; (iii) Pipelines, pumps and filtration systems; (iv) Road, rail, waterway and pipeline transportation facilities; (v) Technical documentation and records retained for post-market inspection; (vi) Transitional provisions for existing petroleum terminals and equipment; (vii) Responsibilities of organizations, individuals and competent authorities in implementation of the Regulation.
productsFreeText:
Equipment, auxiliaries and means used for blending, storing and transporting fuel ethanol and E10 ethanol-blended gasoline (gasohol E10) at petroleum depots/distribution terminals, including:

  • Storage tanks (vertical fixed-roof, internal floating-roof and horizontal cylindrical tanks), floating-roof seals, pressure-vacuum breather valves and tank bottom linings;
  • Process pipelines, pipeline filters and strainers, joint sealants, sealing tapes and gaskets;
  • Pumps and pump filters at pumping stations;
  • Means of transport: road tank vehicles, railway tank wagons, tank compartments of ships and barges, and transport pipelines;
  • Metallic, elastomeric and plastic materials of parts in contact with fuel ethanol or E10 gasoline;
  • Level-gauging pastes and water-finding pastes.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine “Certain Issues Regarding the Retail of Veterinary Medicinal Products at a Distance”
description:
The draft Order provides for the approval of the graphic design of the logo used to identify a veterinary medicinal product market operator authorised to retail veterinary medicinal products at a distance, the technical requirements for the graphic design of the logo and the procedure for its use.

The technical requirements specify the colour values for reproducing the logo, the placement and technical description of the State Flag of Ukraine as part of the logo, the colour values for reproducing the State Flag of Ukraine, the requirements concerning the language of the text displayed on the logo, and the minimum width of the logo.

The procedure for the use of the logo requires a two-way link between the website of a veterinary medicinal product market operator authorised to retail veterinary medicinal products at a distance and the relevant webpage on the official website of the licensing authority listing the operators authorised to retail veterinary medicinal products at a distance.

The draft Order also provides for the approval of a graphic representation of the logo for use on a coloured background.

title: Substantial Product Hazard List: Amendments to Requirements for Window Covering Cords
description: Notice of proposed rulemaking - To address window covering cord strangulation risks, the Commission proposes to designate certain window coverings a substantial product hazard. These include products with: accessible free hanging operating cords longer than 8 inches on custom window coverings; exposed continuous loops with and without tension devices on custom horizontal blinds; exposed continuous loops without tension devices on other custom window coverings; lack of a warning on exposed continuous loops and single retractable cords on custom window coverings; presence of stroke lengths longer than 36 inches on single retractable cord lift systems on custom window coverings; and a cord loop lift system on stock or custom roll up style shades.

title: Draft Decree on steel quality management
description:
1. This draft Decree prescribes specific quality management requirements for steel products and goods in production, importation, and market circulation; post–market quality inspection of steel at the source; and the responsibilities of relevant agencies, organizations, and individuals. 
2. Issues concerning the classification of products and goods based on risk levels; declaration of applicable standards; conformity assessment; declaration of conformity with standards and technical regulations; registration, designation, and recognition of conformity assessment bodies; state inspection of quality; exemption from, reduction of, or intensified inspection; labeling; and the issuance of warnings regarding, recall, and handling of non-conforming products and goods shall be implemented in accordance with the law on standards and technical regulations, the law on product and goods quality, and other relevant laws, except where this Decree provides specific regulations.
3. This draft Decree applies to:
- Organizations and individuals that manufacture, import, or trade in steel products, as well as other organizations and individuals participating in the steel product supply chain in Vietnam.
- Conformity assessment bodies and accreditation bodies with activities related to steel products.
- State management agencies, state inspection agencies for product and goods quality, customs authorities, market surveillance agencies, and other relevant specialized agencies.
- Other agencies, organizations, and individuals involved in steel quality management.

title: Draft Decree of the Head of BPJPH on the Guidelines for the Implementation of the Halal Product Assurance System for Processing Services
description: The guidelines establish a reference for Business Actors for the implementation of the Halal Product Assurance System (SJPH) for Processing Services related to food, beverages, drugs, and cosmetics. The guidelines cover processing services, including contract manufacturing (maklon), shared kitchens, water processing, milling, and other processing services, and set requirements concerning halal commitment and responsibility, materials, Halal Product Processes (PPH), production facilities, packaging and labelling, traceability, internal audits, and management review. The guidelines are intended to assist Business Actors and other relevant stakeholders in ensuring that Processing Services comply with Islamic law and the requirements of the Halal Product Assurance System.

title: Draft Law of Ukraine "On Amendments to Certain Laws of Ukraine Concerning the Regulation of the Circulation of Medicines"
description:
The draft Law proposes to amend the legislation of Ukraine in the field of medicines, including the Laws of Ukraine “On Medicines” and “On Administrative Services”, in order to establish a new regulatory model while ensuring continuity of relevant state functions and preventing interruptions or undue delays in procedures in the field of medicinal products.

The amendments to the Law of Ukraine “On Medicines”, in particular, concern:
shortening the overall timeframe for a decision on the state registration (re-registration) of a medicinal product or refusal of such registration (re-registration) from 210 to 180 calendar days;
improving the provisions concerning the demonstration of bioequivalence of generic medicinal products;
improving the legal framework for clinical trials of medicinal products, including through scientific consultations for applicants on clinical trial-related matters and establishing statutory limits on the cost of the relevant services;
expanding the Bolar exemption by allowing the necessary studies, trials, assessments and other activities required for the state registration of a medicinal product, health technology assessment, state price regulation, reimbursement and preparation for participation in public procurement procedures before the expiry of the relevant patent or supplementary protection certificate (SPC), without allowing the placing on the market or commercial use of the respective medicinal product before the expiry of the relevant intellectual property right;
improving the pharmacovigilance system by regulating the submission and assessment of Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs) for medicinal products registered in Ukraine, implementing the European Union Single Assessment (PSUSA) procedure, and introducing the assessment of post-authorisation safety study (PASS) protocols and substantial amendments thereto;
improving the legal regulation of pharmacy and hospital pharmacy activities and state regulation of prices for medicinal products, including by ensuring the functioning of the National Price Catalogue and improving the mechanisms for the declaration and review of prices for medicinal products;
improving mechanisms for responding to risks of shortages of medicinal products and ensuring continuity of their supply through special measures in circumstances that may affect the availability of medicinal products;
improving transitional provisions concerning medicinal products registered before the entry into force of the new legislation and clinical trials authorised before the entry into force of the Law, including by maintaining the possibility of placing on the market medicinal products registered under the legislation previously in force for the period specified by the transitional provisions, and allowing the completion of clinical trials authorised before the entry into force of the Law.
The draft Law also proposes to amend the Law of Ukraine “On Administrative Services” in order to exclude relations in the field of state regulation of the circulation of medicinal products from its scope.

title: Order of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 7417 "On Approval of the Requirements for Preserved Tuna and Bonito" of 9 July 2026
description:
The Order approves the Requirements for preserved tuna and bonito, which establish standards governing the placing on the market of preserved tuna (Thunnus) and bonito (Bonito) to ensure adequate consumer information and prevent business practices that mislead consumers.

The Requirements establish conditions for the use of food names, specify the fish species that may be used for tuna and bonito, and prohibit the mixing of different fish species in one package unit, except in the case of products of culinary preparation containing a specified minimum content of tuna, bonito or their mixture. They also establish requirements for the forms of presentation of the products and for the liquid medium used in preserved products, including requirements for the corresponding designations in the name of the food product.

The name of the food product must comply with the established requirements and, as applicable, include the fish species, the form of presentation and a description of the liquid medium. The simultaneous use of the names “tuna” and “bonito” in the name of the food product is prohibited. The Requirements also establish minimum fish content depending on the form of presentation and the liquid medium used.

The Order provides that preserved tuna and bonito that comply with the legislation on food safety and certain quality parameters applicable before the entry into force of this Order, but do not comply with all or certain provisions of the Requirements for preserved tuna and bonito approved by this Order, may remain on the market until the expiry of their minimum durability date or use-by date.

title: Draft QCVN 03:2026/BCA – National technical regulation on Fire protection and Rescue equipment
description:
This draft national technical regulation specifies mandatory technical requirements, test methods and sample specifications for fire prevention, firefighting and rescue equipment.

The draft applies to equipment manufactured, assembled, imported, traded and used in Viet Nam (Section 1.1) — unlike the previously notified draft (G/TBT/N/VNM/400), imported equipment is now within the mandatory scope of this regulation.

The draft sets out a conformity assessment mechanism — certification of conformity, declaration of conformity, and post-market surveillance — for equipment classified as medium- or high-risk under the list issued by the Ministry of Public Security, replacing the circulation permit mechanism under the previously notified draft. It further sets out requirements on sampling, testing, labelling and traceability.

This draft applies to: (1) organizations and individuals manufacturing, assembling, importing, trading in and using the equipment; (2) conformity assessment bodies; (3) competent state management authorities.

The first draft of QCVN 03:2026/BCA was notified under G/TBT/N/VNM/400 (23 April 2026). This notification concerns the second draft, which has been substantially revised — reducing the equipment covered from 85 types/865 technical criteria to 57 types/483 technical criteria, and replacing the circulation-permit management mechanism with conformity assessment, information declaration and post-market surveillance.

title:
General Measure No 0111-OOP-C106-26 – metrological and technical requirements for the type approval, verification and testing of specified measuring instruments:
‘measuring systems for determining the energy value of energy gases and their mixtures’
description:
The regulation lays down the metrological and technical requirements for these specified measuring instruments, including the test methods for type approval and verification of specified measuring instruments.

 

Measuring systems for determining the energy value of energy gases and their mixtures may be placed on the market and put into use in the Czech Republic as specified measuring instruments pursuant to Act No 505/1990 on metrology, as amended. Pursuant to this Act, specified measuring instruments are instruments that are included in the list of the types of specified measuring instruments (Decree No 345/2002) and, at the same time, intended (by the manufacturer/importer) for measurements relevant to the protection of public interests in consumer protection, contractual relations, imposition of sanctions, fees, tariffs and taxes, health protection, environmental protection, occupational safety, or the protection of other public interests protected by special legislation. This is therefore a purpose similar to the one defining specified products – non-automatic measuring instruments and scales pursuant to Directives 2014/31/EU and 2014/32/EU. The requirements of this legislation do not apply to measuring instruments not placed on the market in the Czech Republic for the above purposes, defined by Act No 505/1990 on metrology, as amended.
The purpose of this notified legislation is to lay down metrological and technical requirements for these specified measuring instruments. This legislation also stipulates tests for type approval and verification of specified measuring instruments of this type.

This measure of a general nature has been drawn up with a view to achieving the specified objective, whilst taking the greatest possible account of international standards and other generally accepted principles and norms.

Act No 505/1990 on metrology assumes that, for the types of specified measuring instruments listed in the Annex to Decree No 345/2002 laying down the measuring instruments subject to mandatory verification and those subject to type approval, the technical and metrological requirements, including tests for the purposes of type approval, verification and checking of specified measuring instruments, shall be specified in a measure of a general nature.

Given the intended purpose, the stipulated requirements are designed to be as minimal as possible. Moreover, from the manufacturer's point of view, they replicate the usual requirements of normative regulations for products. For manufacturers or users, the type-approval or verification process simply involves demonstrating that the relevant requirements have been met. In addition, the manufacturer does not necessarily have to undergo all the tests at the time of type-approval, if they have already been carried out. The general principle of recognition applies where the requirements are met.

title: Proposal for a Commission Delegated Regulation supplementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 of the European Parliament and of the Council by establishing a list of countries to which the OECD Decision does not apply and to which exports of certain non-hazardous wastes and mixtures of non-hazardous wastes from the Union for recovery are authorised.
description:
Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 on shipments of waste (Article 41) introduced a prohibition on the export of non-hazardous waste from the EU to non-OECD countries, which will enter into force on 21 May 2027. The Regulation also provides for the possibility to derogate from this prohibition for countries that have applied to be included in a list (established by the European Commission) and that have demonstrated the exported waste will be managed in an environmentally sound manner in their territory, with human health, climate and environmental protection requirements equivalent to those of the EU. Article 42 and Annex VIII of the Regulation lay down the application procedure and the information the countries needed to provide in their application.

The European Commission assessed the applications and proposes this draft Delegated Regulation to establish the list of countries to which the OECD Decision does not apply and to which exports of non-hazardous wastes and mixtures of non-hazardous wastes from the Union for recovery are authorised, in accordance with Article 41.

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
The export of waste can create serious environmental, climate and public health damage if the waste is not managed in an environmentally sound manner in the countries of destination. 

In this regard, Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 introduced a prohibition on the export of hazardous and non-hazardous waste from the European Union to non-OECD countries. A derogation to the export ban on non-hazardous waste may only be possible if the country demonstrates sustainable waste management and if the waste is exported for recovery purposes, thereby excluding landfilling or improper disposal and excluding interim operations as per Article 40(2). 

Based on these environmental requirements, this draft Delegated Regulation establishes a list of non-OECD countries to which exports of certain non-hazardous waste are authorized. In order to avoid adverse impacts resulting from the shipment of such waste, this list is to be regularly updated by the European Commission, and at least every two years. The Commission may request additional information from those countries to demonstrate that they continue complying with the requirements set out in Article 42 of the Regulation.

The establishment of this list of non-OECD countries should facilitate the environmentally sound management of waste, in accordance with the waste hierarchy laid down in Article 4 of Directive 2008/98/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council and contribute to the reduction of overall impacts of resource use, which is crucial for the transition to a circular economy

title: Amendments to Regulation 391 and deletion of Table I and Table II of the Twenty-Third Schedule of the Food Regulations 1985 [P.U. (A) 437/1985]
description:
The proposed amendments to Regulation 391 of the Food Regulations 1985 [P.U.(A) 437/1985] are as follows:

  1. subregulations 391(3) to 391(6) are to amend the term "processed cereal based food" to "processed cereal-based food";
  2. subregulations 391(8)(a) and 391(8)(b) are to amend the amount of added carbohydrates from sucrose, fructose, glucose, glucose syrup or honey to products mentioned in subregulations 391(1)(c)(i), 391(1)(c)(ii) and 391(1)(c)(iv);
  3. subregulation 391(9) is to substitute the word "lipid" with "fat";
  4. subregulation 391(14) is to delete provisions relating to food additives and to insert provisions on flavourings in processed cereal-based foods for infants and young children;
  5. subregulation 391(15) is to delete provision on food conditioner in processed cereal-based foods for infants and young children;
  6. subregulation 391(17)(b)(i) is to amend nutrition labelling in processed cereal-based foods for infants and young children;
  7. subregulation 391(21) is to delete provision on contaminants in processed cereal-based foods for infants and young children;
  8. Table I of the Twenty-Third Schedule is to delete the list of permitted food additives and its maximum level in processed cereal-based foods for infants and young children; and
  9. Table II of the Twenty-Third Schedule is to delete the list of permitted food additives in processed cereal-based foods for infants and young children.

title:
Proposed scheduling decision - Long chain perfluorocarboxylic acids (LC PFCAs) (PDF 322 KB)

Proposed scheduling decision - Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) (PDF 344 KB) 

(8 page(s), in English), (9 page(s), in English)
description:
The Industrial Chemicals Environmental Management Standard (IChEMS) has been developed by all Australian governments to efficiently and effectively manage the risks of industrial chemicals to the environment, while providing consistent requirements for businesses across Australia. The IChEMS Register records standards for the environmental management of chemicals, including risk management measures for specific industrial uses. In turn, the Australian federal government and each state and territory government will enact legislation to implement the standards in their jurisdictions.

The proposed standards will assign the following chemicals, and mixtures and articles containing the chemicals, to Schedule 6 of the IChEMS Register. This will prohibit their import, manufacture, use and export in Australia, with exceptions for some essential uses, unintentional trace contamination, research, environmentally sound disposal, and articles in use prior to the standards' date of entry into force.

•          Long chain perfluorocarboxylic acids (LC PFCAs)

•          Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)

The essential uses in the proposed standards broadly align with the exceptions in the Stockholm Convention (for LC PFCAs) and the Montreal Protocol (for HFCs). Australia has opted to not include the Montreal Protocol exception for car air conditioning in the essential uses for HFCs, based on the global trend toward not allowing this exception.
productsFreeText:
Long chain perfluorocarboxylic acids (LC PFCAs), with the molecular formula of CnF2n+1COOH (where 8 ≤ n ≤ 20)

Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), the molecular formula CnH(2n+2–x)Fx, where 1 ≤ n ≤ 5, and where a) for n = 1, x = 1-3, b) for n = 2, x = 2-5, c) for n = 3, x = 2-7, d) for n = 4, x = 3-9, e) for n = 5, x = 10-11
objectivesFreeText:
• Achieve better protection of the environment through improved management of the environmental risks posed by industrial chemicals.
  • Provide a nationally consistent, transparent, predictable and streamlined approach to environmental risk management of industrial chemicals for governments, industry and the community.

Australia has opted to not include the Montreal Protocol exception for car air conditioning in the essential uses for HFCs, based on the global trend toward not allowing this exception.

title: Proyecto de Norma Oficial Mexicana PROY-NOM-007-ENER-2026, Eficiencia energética para sistemas de alumbrado en edificios no residenciales.
description: The notified draft Standard seeks to establish the energy-efficiency levels, expressed in terms of the electrical power density for lighting, that non-residential building lighting systems must meet, including the method for calculating that density. This is intended to ensure that these systems are designed and constructed in an energy-efficient manner by optimizing their design and using state-of-the-art technologies, such as LED lighting, without compromising the required illuminance levels.G/TBT/N/MEX/582- 2 -
productsFreeText: Aplica a los sistemas de alumbrado interior y exterior de los edificios no residenciales nuevos, así como a las ampliaciones y modificaciones delos sistemas de alumbrado interior y exterior de los edificios existentes dentro del territorio de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos. Los inmuebles cubiertos por esta regulación son aquellos cuyos usos autorizados queden comprendidos dentro de los tipos siguientes: oficinas; escuelas y demás centros docentes; establecimientos comerciales; hospitales; hoteles; restaurantes; bodegas; recreación y cultura; talleres de servicio; y centrales de pasajeros.

title: Communiqué Amending the Communiqué on Warning Messages to be Placed on Alcoholic Beverage Packaging
description:
The Draft Communiqué proposes changing the warning phrase "Alcohol is not your friend” found in Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the Communiqué on Warning Messages to be Placed on Alcoholic Beverage Packaging (published in the Official Gazette dated 11 August 2013 and numbered 28732) to "Alcohol can cause cancer."

 

Furthermore, the Draft Communiqué envisages updating the packaging and warning regulations (Article 3/1/d) which were previously notified to the WTO under G/TBT/N/TUR/41 and its subsequent addendum (G/TBT/N/TUR/41/Add.1 and G/TBT/N/TUR/41/Add.2) as well as modifying mandatory QR code placement requirements and the dimensions of warning messages.

 

This Communiqué shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

 

PROVISIONAL ARTICLE 1 – Except for products manufactured for export purposes, the production, importation, and placing on the domestic market by manufacturers and importers of products that do not meet the requirements set forth in Articles 2 and 3 of this Communiqué shall be prohibited as of six months after the date of entry into force of the Communiqué introducing this Article.

According to the Law, secondary legislation concerning aforementioned paragraph of Article 2, has to enter into force within 2 months after the publication of the Law, that is, as of August 11, 2013.</span></span></p><p><span style="font-size:x-small;font-face:Verdana;"></span></p><p><span style="font-size:x-small;font-face:Verdana;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-size:9pt;">Therefore, the Communiqué on Warning Messages Placed on Containers of Alcoholic Beverages was prepared.</span></span></p><p><span style="font-size:x-small;font-face:Verdana;"></span></p><span style="font-size:x-small;font-face:Verdana;"><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:'Verdana','sans-serif';font-size:9pt;">The objective of this Communiqué is to protect unborn children and minors and to prevent driving under the influence of alcohol. </span></span>

title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Manufactured Housing
description:
In this notification, the U.S. Department of Energy (''DOE'' or ''the Department'') is providing notice that the Department's Energy Conservation Standards for Manufactured Housing final rule (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/521/Add.9) published in the Federal Register on 31 May 2022, has no legal effect in light of the enactment of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (''ROAD Act'').

 

The information contained in this notification will be applicable on 18 September 2026 and will remain in effect until further notice.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 59048, 18 September 2026; Title 10 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 460:

Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for 
Manufactured Housing
descriptionPlain:
In this notification, the U.S. Department of Energy (''DOE'' or ''the Department'') is providing notice that the Department's Energy Conservation Standards for Manufactured Housing final rule (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/521/Add.9) published in the Federal Register on 31 May 2022, has no legal effect in light of the enactment of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (''ROAD ActThe information contained in this notification will be applicable on 18 September 2026 and will remain in effect until further notice.91 Federal Register (FR) 59048, 18 September 2026; Title 10 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 460
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-18/html/2026-19154.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-18/pdf/2026-19154.pdfThis notification of legal effect and previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/521 are identified by Docket Number EERE-2009-BT-BC-0021. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/EERE-2009-BT-BC-0021/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number.

title: Reglamento Técnico Salvadoreño RTS 75.02.04:26 DISTRIBUCIÓN DE GAS NATURAL POR REDES. DISEÑO, CONSTRUCCIÓN, OPERACIÓN, MANTENIMIENTO Y ABANDONO O DESACTIVACIÓN.
description: The notified Salvadoran Technical Regulation establishes the technical requirements for designing and building the infrastructure for natural gas network distribution systems, as well as the conditions for the operation, maintenance, inspection, and abandonment or decommissioning of those networks. It applies exclusively to natural gas network distribution systems and covers the following activities: - The design of piping installations in natural gas networks, up to the outer boundary of the residential service, at the point where they enter the metering and regulating box or cabinet. - The construction or repair of natural gas distribution networks or supply branches installed in the public right-of-way and operating at a maximum pressure of 4,200 kPa (42 bar). - The performance of work and the minimum safety conditions applicable to the construction, operation, and maintenance of natural gas distribution systems. It also establishes environmental protection requirements to be met during such work.

title: Draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine “On Amendments to Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 980 of  29 July 2026” (related to the labelling of food and feed)
description:
The revised draft Resolution proposes specific rules concerning the labelling and circulation of imported food products under Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 980 of 29 July 2026 "On Repealing Certain Resolutions of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Concerning the Labelling of Food and Feed", in particular:

during martial law, food products for special medical purposes and infant food imported to Ukraine as humanitarian aid, for which information is provided in a language other than the state language, may remain in circulation in Ukraine until the end of their minimum durability date or use-by date. The circulation of such food products is permitted exclusively to recipients and/or beneficiaries of humanitarian aid;

until 1 April 2027, prepacked imported food products for which the mandatory information on the packaging or label is provided in a language other than the state language, may be imported to Ukraine, placed on the market and sold, provided that:

consignments of prepacked imported food products are accompanied, at all stages of the food chain, by complete information on the food products, in accordance with the requirements of the Law of Ukraine "On Information for Consumers on Food Products", provided in the state language in paper and/or electronic form;

a food market operator that sells prepacked imported food products to the final consumer provides the consumer, free of charge and before purchase, with access to the mandatory information on the food product in the state language by one of the following means, at the operator’s choice: displaying the information directly at the place where the food product is sold or next to it; displaying a QR code on the price tag or shelf, packaging, or another physical medium located directly next to the food product; using an electronic price tag, information terminal or another electronic device at the place where the food product is sold; displaying the information on the website or in the mobile application of the food market operator; providing the information in printed form or by another means that ensures the consumer has free access to such information;

in the case of distance selling, the mandatory information on the food product in the state language, except for information on the minimum durability date or use-by date, is available to the consumer before the completion of the order, while the complete information is provided upon delivery.

Prepacked imported food products referred to above that are placed on the market before 1 April 2027 may remain in circulation in Ukraine until the end of their minimum durability date or use-by date.

The revised draft Resolution also removes the provision providing that this Resolution shall enter into force on 1 October 2026.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine "On Amendments to the Order of the Ministry for Development of Economy, Trade and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 741 of 12 April 2021" (concerning Hygienic Requirements for the production and circulation of natural mineral water and spring water)
description:
The draft Order provides for amendments to the Hygienic Requirements for the Production and Circulation of Natural Mineral Waters and Spring Waters, approved by Order of the Ministry for Development of Economy, Trade and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 741 of 12 April 2021, notified in documents G/TBT/N/UKR/185 and G/TBT/N/UKR/185/Add.1.
The draft Order establishes technical requirements for the treatment of natural mineral waters and spring waters with ozone-enriched air and activated alumina, including requirements concerning the use of these treatment methods and the quality control of activated alumina.
It also establishes labelling requirements for treated natural mineral waters and spring waters, including the indication of the adsorption method used.
The draft Order has been developed based on the provisions of Commission Directive 2003/40/EC and Commission Regulation (EU) No 115/2010.
It is also notified under the SPS Agreement, as it contains measures aimed at ensuring the safety of the treatment of natural mineral waters and spring waters and preventing changes to their essential characteristics.

title: Partial Repeal of the Carbon Pollution Standards for Fossil Fuel- Fired Electric Generating Units
description:
In this final rule, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is repealing most provisions of the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards for greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs) based on a reevaluation of the best system of emission reduction for the relevant subcategories. Specifically, the EPA is repealing the emission guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired steam generating units, the carbon capture and sequestration/storage (CCS)-based standards for coal-fired steam generating units undertaking a large modification, and the CCS-based standards for new base load stationary combustion turbines (i.e., Phase 2 standards). In a separate action published concurrently with this final rule, the EPA is issuing a supplemental proposal soliciting comment on additional reasons to rescind all GHG emission requirements for fossil fuel-fired EGUs to effectuate the best reading of Clean Air Act (CAA) section 111 and ensure consistency with applicable principles of administrative law beyond those reasons on which the EPA solicited comment in the June 2025 notice of proposed rulemaking (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2220).

 

This final rule is effective on 16 November 2026. The approval of the Director of the Federal Register (FR) for incorporation by reference (IBR) of certain material listed in this rule expires as of 16 November 2026.

title: Rescission of the Greenhouse Gas Findings for Fossil Fuel-Fired Power Plants and Repeal of Regulations for Power Plant Greenhouse Gas Emissions Under Clean Air Act Section 111
description:
In this action, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is supplementing its proposal to repeal all greenhouse gas (GHG) emission standards for fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs) to effectuate the best reading of Clean Air Act (CAA) section 111. We propose that CAA section 111 does not authorize the EPA to regulate emissions from power plants in response to global climate change concerns. For the multiple and independent reasons described herein, this additional rationale would also require rescinding the Administrator's contrary findings and determinations in 2015 and repealing all associated 2015 and 2024 GHG standards for the fossil fuel-fired EGU source category. In a separate action published concurrently with this supplemental notice, the EPA is finalizing the repeal of certain 2024 GHG standards for the fossil fuel-fired EGU source category on distinct legal and technical grounds. We are not reopening that final rule. Nor are we soliciting further comment on those issues through this supplemental notice, except to the extent that commenters believe the final rule bears on the distinct questions of statutory authority addressed herein.

 

Comments must be received on or before 2 November 2026. Comments on the information collection provisions submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) under the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) are best assured of consideration by OMB if OMB receives a copy of your comments on or before 19 October 2026. Please refer to the PRA section under ''Statutory and E.O. Reviews'' in this preamble for specific instructions.    

 

The EPA will hold a virtual public hearing on 1 October 2026. The EPA will announce further details at https://www.epa.gov/stationary-sources-air-pollution/greenhouse-gas-standards-and-guidelines-fossil-fuel-fired-power. Please refer to the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section for information on registering for the public hearing.

title: Revocation of Obsolete Rules Regarding Infant Bouncer Seats and Stationary Activity Centers
description:
The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (Commission or CPSC) is withdrawing a direct final rule (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2304) that would remove two obsolete rules concerning infant bouncer seats and stationary activity centers that was published in the Federal Register on 22 July 2026, because the Commission received a significant adverse comment.

 

The direct final rule published on 22 July 2026 (91 FR 45992) is withdrawn effective 17 September 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 58817, 17 September 2026; Title 16 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 1500:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-17/html/2026-19065.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-17/pdf/2026-19065.pdf

 

This withdrawal and the direct final rule notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2304 are identified by Docket Number CPSC-2026-0298. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/CPSC-2026-0298/document and provides access to primary documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number.

title: Draft revision of the ordinance on energy efficiency
description:
As part of the present revision of the Energy Efficiency Ordinance of November 1, 2017 (EnEV; SR 730.02), adaptations to EU law are being made.

Energy efficiency requirements are adapted to EU law in Annexes 1.18 (Local Space Heaters) and 2.2 (external power supplies). The existing exception to EU law in Annex 2.14 is being partially revised and tightened. Commercial deep fryers are now required to automatically lower the temperature when not in use.

Amendments to exhaust gas regulations for diesel-fueled special large motor vehicles and special small motor vehicles with a maximum engine output ranging from 19 kW to 560 kW are proposed as follows:

i) Introduction of Particle Number (PN) emission standards; and

title: Mandatory Implementation of the Indonesian National Standard for Wheat Flour
description: Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 61 of 2024 has been revised by Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 21 of 2026 regarding Mandatory Implementation of Indonesia National Standard for Wheat Fluor for Food Use. The amendment revises the requirements for mandatory SNI certification of wheat flour for food use. Key changes include expanding the eligible business classification codes for repackers to KBLI 10616, 82920, and/or 82922; removing the requirement for repackers to maintain sieving facilities; and explicitly exempting repackers from testing equipment requirements. Domestic industrial companies may submit a declaration of implementation of ISO 9001:2015 and/or a food safety management system without the previous one-year business licensing restriction. The requirement to obtain the corresponding management system certificate by the second surveillance is also removed, while the trademark certificate requirement remains. Minimum audit durations are reduced to two person-days for repackers’ initial certification and recertification, and for domestic surveillance audits. The certification scheme is updated accordingly. SNI 3751:2018 and the Type 5 certification scheme remain unchanged. The amendment entered into force on 31 July 2026.

titlePlain: Mandatory Implementation of the Indonesian National Standard for Wheat Flour
descriptionPlain: Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 61 of 2024 has been revised by Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 21 of 2026 regarding Mandatory Implementation of Indonesia National Standard for Wheat Fluor for Food Use. The amendment revises the requirements for mandatory SNI certification of wheat flour for food use. Key changes include expanding the eligible business classification codes for repackers to KBLI 10616, 82920, and/or 82922; removing the requirement for repackers to maintain sieving facilities; and explicitly exempting repackers from testing equipment requirements. Domestic industrial companies may submit a declaration of implementation of ISO 9001:2015 and/or a food safety management system without the previous one-year business licensing restriction. The requirement to obtain the corresponding management system certificate by the second surveillance is also removed, while the trademark certificate requirement remains. Minimum audit durations are reduced to two person-days for repackers’ initial certification and recertification, and for domestic surveillance audits. The certification scheme is updated accordingly. SNI 3751:2018 and the Type 5 certification scheme remain unchanged. The amendment entered into force on 31 July 2026.

title: Mandatory Implementation of the Indonesian National Standard for Palm Cooking Oil
description: Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 3 of 2025 has been revised by Regulation of Minister of Industry No. 14 of 2026 regarding Mandatory Implementation of Indonesia National Standard for Palm Oil. The amendment revises the requirements for mandatory SNI certification of palm cooking oil, particularly for repackers. Key changes include expanding the eligible business classification codes for repackers to KBLI 10437, 82920, and/or 82922, and replacing the minimum facility requirement for filtration and packaging with storage and packaging facilities. The revised provisions require repackers to own a trademark in Class 29, including collective trademarks, and remove the previously stated alternative of holding a trademark licensing agreement. The certification scheme is revised to reflect these changes. SNI 7709:2019 and the Type 5 certification scheme remain unchanged. The amendment entered into force on 23 June 2026.

description:
New Zealand has amended Schedules 1AA and 2A of the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 and Schedule 1 of the Imports and Exports (Restrictions) Prohibition Order (No 2) 2004 to implement decisions made by the 2025 Conference of the Parties under the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, to which New Zealand is a Party. 

New Zealand has prohibited from use and production two chemicals, MCCPs (plasticiser and flame retardant) and LC-PFCAs (PFAS with a number of applications, including surface treatments and consumer products). 

These prohibitions are subject to some specific exemptions allowing the continued use of the substances, aligning with the specific use exemptions available under the Stockholm Convention. All exemptions are time-limited and are set out in detail in the accompanying statutory instrument.
productsFreeText:
Medium-chain chlorinated paraffins:

“Medium-chain chlorinated paraffins (MCCPs)” means substances that contain either or both of the following:

  1. Linear chloroalkanes with carbon chain lengths in the range C14–17 and chlorination levels at or exceeding 45% chlorine by weight:
  2. linear C14–17 chloroalkanes of the molecular formula C14H(30−y)Cly (where y ≥ 5), C15H(32−y)Cly (where y ≥ 5), C16H(34−y)Cly (where y ≥ 6), or C17H(36−y)Cly (where y ≥ 6)

Unintentional trace contaminants of medium-chain chlorinated paraffins (MCCPs) in products or articles are persistent organic pollutants if the total concentration of linear C14–17 chloroalkanes, of any of the molecular formulae in paragraph (b) of the above definition, in substances in those products or articles is greater than 3% by weight

MCCPs are used in a wide range of applications, mainly as a secondary plasticiser and flame retardant in polyvinyl chloride (PVC), as extreme pressure additives in metalworking fluids, and as additives to paints, adhesives, sealants, rubbers and other polymeric materials.

 

Long-chain perfluorocarboxylic acids, their salts, and related compounds:

“Long-chain perfluorocarboxylic acids” or “their salts” means a homologous series of substances with the molecular formula of CnF2n+1COOH (where 8 ≤ n ≤ 20)

“Related compounds” means any substance that is a precursor and may transform to long-chain perfluorocarboxylic acids, where the perfluorinated alkyl moiety—

  1. has the formula CnF2n+1 (where 8 ≤ n ≤ 20); and
  2. is directly bonded to any chemical moiety other than a fluorine, chlorine, or bromine atom

“Long-chain perfluorocarboxylic acids, their salts, and related compounds” does not include perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), its salts, and PFOA-related compounds as listed in this Schedule

LC-PFCAs are used in a wide range of applications, including industrial uses, electronic articles, medical and laboratory devices, food contact materials, paints, fire-fighting foams, personal care products and the automotive industry.

objectives.name: Protection of animal or plant life or health (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
POPs are substances which meet four criteria: they are persistent, toxic, bioaccumulative, and they have the potential for environmental transport far away from sources of emissions, including across international borders. POPs have been used in various products including pesticides and industrial chemicals and released during chemical and agriculture processes. New Zealand is a party to the Stockholm Convention, which aims to prohibit, eliminate or restrict the production and use of persistent organic pollutants (POPs).

New Zealand is prohibiting chemicals which have been found to be environmentally harmful and have been adopted by UN Stockholm Convention for global elimination to protect human health and the environment.

Therefore, this intervention is necessary to protect human and animal life and health, and the environment. To meet our international obligations under the Stockholm Convention we must implement restrictions on MCCPs and LC-PFCAs by 16 December 2026.

title: BOS 78:2013 Unplasticized polyvinyl chloride (PVC-U) soil, waste and vent pipes and pipe fittings — Specification
description:
This Botswana Standard specifies requirements for unplasticized poly vinyl chloride (PVC-U) pipes (including vent pipes) and pipe fittings of nominal sizes 40 mm to 160 mm intended for above-ground non-pressure applications for the conveyance of soil (human excrement or faeces) and waste water where continuous temperatures in excess of 60 °C are not encountered.
The standard specifies requirements for fittings manufactured predominantly by the injection-moulding process but does not cover fittings produced by fabrication.
The standard also gives guidance on jointing of pipes by means of solvent cement and by means of rubber joint rings.

title:
Measure of a general nature number: 0111-OOP-C105-26 - metrological and technical requirements, test methods for type approval, verification and checking:
‘temperature measuring instruments used on stationary tanks for conversion to reference conditions – temperature sensors and temperature sensors with a transducer’
description:
The regulation lays down the metrological and technical requirements for these specified measuring instruments, including the test methods for type approval and verification of specified measuring instruments.

 

Temperature measuring instruments used on stationary tanks for conversion to reference conditions – temperature sensors and temperature sensors with a transducer may be placed on the market and put into service in the Czech Republic as specified measuring instruments pursuant to Act No 505/1990 on metrology, as amended. Pursuant to this Act, specified measuring instruments are instruments that are included in the list of the types of specified measuring instruments (Decree No 345/2002) and, at the same time, intended (by the manufacturer/importer) for measurements of relevance to the protection of public interests in areas of consumer protection, contractual relations, imposition of sanctions, fees, tariffs and taxes, health protection, environmental protection, occupational safety, or the protection of other public interests protected by special legislation. This is therefore a purpose similar to the one defining specified products – non-automatic measuring instruments and scales pursuant to Directives 2014/31/EU and 2014/32/EU. The requirements of this legislation do not apply to measuring instruments not placed on the market in the Czech Republic for the above purposes, defined by Act No 505/1990 on metrology, as amended.
The purpose of this notified legislation is to lay down metrological and technical requirements for these specified measuring instruments. This legislation also stipulates tests for type approval and verification of specified measuring instruments of this type.

 

This measure of a general nature has been drawn up with a view to achieving the specified objective, whilst taking the greatest possible account of international standards and other generally accepted principles and norms.

Act No 505/1990 on metrology assumes that, for the types of specified measuring instruments listed in the Annex to Decree No 345/2002 laying down the measuring instruments subject to mandatory verification and those subject to type approval, the technical and metrological requirements, including tests for the purposes of type approval, verification and checking of specified measuring instruments, shall be specified in a measure of a general nature.
 

Given the intended purpose, the stipulated requirements are designed to be as minimal as possible. Moreover, from the manufacturer's point of view, they replicate the usual requirements of normative regulations for products. For manufacturers or users, the type-approval or verification process simply involves demonstrating that the relevant requirements have been met. In addition, the manufacturer does not necessarily have to undergo all the tests at the time of type-approval, if they have already been carried out. The general principle of recognition applies where the requirements are met.

title: Proposal for Amendments to the Legal Inspection Requirements for Fuel Containers Pre-filled with Liquefied Petroleum Gas for Portable Butane Gas Stoves, Torches or General Refillable Lighters
description:
Fuel containers pre-filled with liquefied petroleum gas for portable butane gas stoves, torches or general refillable lighters have been subject to mandatory inspection by the BSMI since 1 January 2003. The current conformity assessment procedure is Type-Approved Batch Inspection, and the applicable inspection standard is CNS 14530:2014. The labeling requirements for fuel containers for torches or general refillable lighters are prescribed in Section 9 of CNS 12951:2003.

The revised CNS 14530:2023, in Section 9.6 and Annex B, introduces pressure-resistance test requirements for fuel containers for portable butane gas stoves equipped with pressure relief devices. In addition, the labeling requirements in Section 10(a) of the revised CNS 12951:2016 no longer include the requirement specified in Item (5) of Section 9 of CNS 12951:2003 concerning whether an odorant has been added, and newly require compliance with relevant regulations announced by the competent authority for the relevant industry. Accordingly, the relevant inspection requirements are amended in accordance with the revised inspection standards.

descriptionPlain: Fuel containers pre-filled with liquefied petroleum gas for portable butane gas stoves, torches or general refillable lighters have been subject to mandatory inspection by the BSMI since 1 January 2003. The current conformity assessment procedure is Type-Approved Batch Inspection, and the applicable inspection standard is CNS 14530:2014. The labeling requirements for fuel containers for torches or general refillable lighters are prescribed in Section 9 of CNS 12951:2003.The revised CNS 14530:2023, in Section 9.6 and Annex B, introduces pressure-resistance test requirements for fuel containers for portable butane gas stoves equipped with pressure relief devices. In addition, the labeling requirements in Section 10(a) of the revised CNS 12951:2016 no longer include the requirement specified in Item (5) of Section 9 of CNS 12951:2003 concerning whether an odorant has been added, and newly require compliance with relevant regulations announced by the competent authority for the relevant industry. Accordingly, the relevant inspection requirements are amended in accordance with the revised inspection standards.

title: Proposed Voluntary Product Standard PS 2-25, Performance Standard for Wood Structural Panels
description: Notice of availability; request for comments - The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is distributing for public comment a proposed revision of Voluntary Product Standard PS 2-25, Performance Standard for Wood Structural Panels. The revisions to the standard were coordinated by the APA--The Engineered Wood Association, (formally known as the American Plywood Association), prepared by the Standard Review Committee, and approved by the PS 2 Standing Committee. The proposed standard would establish the physical properties and structural performance criteria for assessing the acceptability of wood structural panels primarily used for construction sheathing and single floor applications and provide a basis for common understanding among the manufacturers, distributors, and users of these products. Interested parties are invited to review the proposed standard and submit comments to NIST.

title: Amending Over-the-Counter Monograph M020: Sunscreen Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use, and Related Information; Aminobenzoic Acid (PABA) and Trolamine Salicylate
description:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability on its website of the final administrative order (final order) (OTC000008-1) titled ''Amending Over-the-Counter Monograph M020: Sunscreen Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use, and Related Information; Aminobenzoic Acid (PABA) and Trolamine Salicylate.'' This final order amends ''Over-the-Counter Monograph M020: Sunscreen Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use'' (Over-the-Counter (OTC) Monograph M020) to remove PABA and trolamine salicylate as sunscreen active ingredients. A sunscreen drug product containing PABA or trolamine salicylate is not generally recognized as safe and effective (GRASE).

 

The announcement of the availability on FDA's website of the final order is published in the Federal Register on 11 September 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 57892, 11 September 2026:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-11/html/2026-18551.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-11/pdf/2026-18551.pdf

https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/omuf/Order/FinalAdministrativeOrderOTC000008-PABATrolamine.pdf

 

This notice of availability is identified by Docket Number FDA-1978-N-0018. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/FDA-1978-N-0018/document and provides access to primary documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number.

 

Previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/1443 are identified by Docket Numbers FDA-1978-N-0018 and FDA-2025-N-6494.

title: Protecting Against National Security Threats to the Communications Supply Chain through the Equipment Authorization Program
description:
In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) takes further steps to strengthen its equipment authorization program against national security risks to the communications supply chain. The Commission closes a component-part loophole by prohibiting authorization of devices that incorporate logic-bearing hardware components produced by an entity identified on the Commission's Covered List, where the device would itself be prohibited from authorization had the Covered List entity produced the entire device. The Commission also requires that any modification or permissive change to equipment by an entity identified on the Covered List undergo full certification, clarifies that its marketing rules reach any entity (including online marketplaces) that markets unauthorized equipment, and requires online marketplaces, subject to limited exceptions, to display a device's FCC ID at the online point of sale. Finally, the Commission amends its definition of ''critical infrastructure,'' as used on the Covered List, and corrects two administrative errors in its rules.

 

This final rule is effective 13 October 2026.

https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-50A1.pdf

 

This final rule and the proposed rule notified as G/TBT/N/USA/1771/Rev.3 are identified by ET Docket No. 21-232; FCC 26-50. The full text of the final rule is available from the Commission's website at https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-50A1.pdf. Documents are also accessible from the FCC's Electronic Document Management System (EDOCS) by searching the ET Docket Number. Comments "filings" and Commission documents are accessible from the FCC’s Electronic Comment Filing System (ECFS) https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs/search/search-filings/results?q=(proceedings.name:(%2221-232%22)).

title: The Measuring Instruments (Display Requirements) (Amendment and Consequential) Regulations 2026
description:
This instrument amends the Measuring Instruments Regulations 2016 (MIR) as they apply in Great Britain (GB) to permit the use of a metrologically controlled remote display, such as a smartphone app. This will offer an alternative option to the existing requirement for an in-built physical display for active electrical energy 
meters (AEEMs) within certain Energy Smart Appliances (ESAs). ESAs include devices such as Electric Vehicle (EV) charge points and heat pumps.

(HS code(s): 902680); Electricity supply or production meters, incl. calibrating meters therefor (HS code(s): 902830)
