objectivesFreeText:
The objective of the notified instrument is to improve the roll out of Energy Smart Appliances in Great Britain, by providing display options for energy measurement meters. This will reduce production costs and improve consumer access to energy flexibility services and so support delivery of Net Zero targets.This change is intended to remove a key barrier to the rollout of ESAs by reducing manufacturing costs and better reflecting modern consumer preferences for accessing information digitally, while maintaining existing safeguards to ensure measurement accuracy, integrity and legal validity. It will support consumers in accessing energy-use information, participating in flexibility services, and making lower-cost and lower-carbon energy choices, contributing to the UK Government’s Net Zero obligations and clean power objectives. 

 

This change will support the new requirements being introduced by the Energy Smart Appliance Regulations 2026 in Great Britain, which will require that from 1 January 2028, all Phase 1 ESAs must incorporate a MIR-compliant Class B AEEM and undergo conformity assessment, ensuring accurate energy measurement while enabling wider deployment of smart energy technologies. The display requirements for other regulated measuring instruments are unaffected. This change is closely aligned to provisions in Directive (EU) 2026/706 which introduce a remote display option for certain measuring instruments, allowing legally relevant information to be provided through a remote display rather than solely through a physical display. This targeted and proportionate approach responds directly to industry concerns that mandatory physical displays create unnecessary costs without providing significant consumer benefits.

title: Draft Decree of the Head of BPJPH on the Guidelines for the Implementation of the Halal Product Assurance System for Medical Devices and Household Health Supplies
description: The guideline establishes requirements for the implementation of the Halal Product Assurance System (SJPH) and halal certification for medical devices and Household Health Supplies (PKRT). It covers medical devices derived from or containing animal-derived materials and/or alcohol that enter or directly contact the human body, limited to those used in religious rituals requiring purity. It also covers PKRT derived from or containing animal-derived materials that directly contact the human body during such rituals, food and beverages, or dining and kitchen utensils. The guideline aims to ensure compliance with applicable halal requirements and maintain halal status throughout the production process in accordance with SJPH criteria and relevant MUI Fatwas

title: DUS 5544:2026, Safety of toys — Age determination guidelines — Specification; First Edition
description:
This Draft Uganda Standard provides an indication of the lowest age at which children start playing with toys in specific toy sub-categories. It is primarily directed to manufacturers and agencies that evaluate the compliance of toys with safety standards.

This Draft Uganda Standard can be used as a reference to determine the appropriateness of toys by earliest age, for use by distributors, institutions and organizations involved with child play, as well as by paediatric institutions, teachers, other professionals that use toys in their routine activities, and consumers.

 

The age at which children develop different abilities is unique for each individual child. This document illustrates the age ranges during which a typical child has developed certain abilities. Although age grading has safety implications, this document is not intended to address specific safety requirements. Specific safety requirements for toys (e.g. restriction of the presence of small parts and small balls in toys intended for certain age groups, due to the choking hazard) can be found in the ISO 8124 series and in other regional toy safety standards and regulations.

title: Draft Law of Ukraine “On Biocidal Products”
description:
The draft Law of Ukraine “On Biocidal Products” establishes a regulatory framework for the approval of active substances used in biocidal products and the state registration, production, making available on the market, placing on the market and use of biocidal products and treated articles. It also defines the rights and obligations of legal entities and individuals, as well as the powers of state authorities and their officials in the field of biocidal products.

Specifically, the draft Law:

establishes procedures for the assessment and approval, renewal or review of approval of active substances used in biocidal products, including the preparation of expert conclusions;
establishes a procedure for the state registration of biocidal products, including under a simplified procedure;
establishes the procedure and criteria for authorizing a state entity to conduct the relevant assessments and provide related services, as well as the duration and withdrawal of such authorization and the procedure for determining the fees for the relevant services;
establishes requirements for laboratories conducting laboratory testing of active substances for the preparation of active substance dossiers, including accreditation requirements;
provides for the establishment of the State Register of Biocidal Products, which is to become operational on 1 January 2030, through the modernization of the existing State Register of Disinfectants;
stipulates that all registrations of disinfectants that are valid as of the date of entry into force of the Law shall remain valid until their expiry;

establishes the classification of biocidal products, as set out in an Annex to the draft Law.

The draft Law also introduces amendments to the Laws of Ukraine “On Protection of the Population from Infectious Diseases” and “On the Public Health System” to ensure consistency of legislation concerning biocidal products.

This draft Law was previously notified in 2025 under the title “On Making Available on the Market and Use of Biocidal Products”.

The draft Law is also notified in accordance with the requirements of the SPS Agreement.

title: Draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine “On Amendments to Certain Technical Regulations Concerning Emergencies in the European Union Internal Market”
description:
The draft Resolution proposes to amend 12 technical regulations developed on the basis of EU harmonisation legislation by introducing a new section setting out procedures applicable in emergency situations following the activation by the European Commission of an emergency situation regime in the EU internal market.

These procedures would allow products covered by the respective technical regulations to be placed on the market and/or put into service where such products have been manufactured in accordance with the requirements of European, international or national standards or common technical specifications additionally identified by the European Commission.

In order to address potential disruptions to the functioning of the EU internal market in the event of an emergency and to ensure the rapid placing on the market of products identified by the European Commission as crisis-relevant goods, the draft Resolution also provides for priority processing by notified bodies of applications for conformity assessment of such products, as well as priority market surveillance of such products.

Furthermore, the draft Resolution provides that, under certain conditions, the placing on the market or putting into service, where applicable, of products covered by the relevant technical regulations may not be restricted where an authorisation for their placing on the market and/or putting into service has been issued by the competent authority of an EU Member State and the European Commission has extended the effect of such authorisation to the territory of all EU Member States.

The amendments to the technical regulations will enter into force on the date of Ukraine’s accession to the European Union, but not earlier than six months after the date of official publication of the Resolution introducing these amendments.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On Approval of the Procedure for Quality Control of Medicines During Wholesale and Retail Trade”
description:
The draft Order proposes to approve a new Procedure for quality control of medicines during wholesale and retail trade, which establishes the mechanism for conducting incoming quality control of medicines by business entities licensed to conduct wholesale and retail trade in medicinal products, as well as for state supervision (control) in the field of medicines during their wholesale and retail trade.

The draft has been developed with the aim of bringing the procedures for quality control of medicines into compliance with Law of Ukraine No. 2469-IX of 28 July 2022 “On Medicines”, updating the relevant terminology, and establishing requirements for ensuring the quality of medicines during their wholesale and retail trade.

The draft Order, in particular:

establishes a 5-year retention period for documents confirming the procurement, storage, transportation, trade, destruction or disposal of medicines;

proposes to include medicinal products not accompanied by a package leaflet in the list of medicines prohibited from sale;

establishes incoming quality control of medicines at receiving areas through visual inspection by authorized persons before a decision is made to release the respective batches for sale;

establishes the procedure for sampling medicines  where doubts arise as to their quality or where falsification is suspected, and for submitting such samples to the territorial bodies of Ukrpharmagency for state laboratory quality control in accordance with Article 108 of Law of Ukraine No. 2469-IX “On Medicines”;

introduces, for business entities engaged in wholesale trade in medicines, a requirement to keep records of medicinal product sales in electronic and/or paper form, including the information necessary to ensure the traceability of each batch and its prompt recall, where necessary;

provides for the possibility of preparing incoming quality control conclusions and maintaining records of the movement and sale of medicines in electronic form using electronic record-keeping systems with user authentication.

The adoption of the draft Order will contribute to ensuring appropriate control over the quality, safety and efficacy of medicines during their wholesale and retail trade, as well as ensuring the traceability of medicinal products at the relevant stages of their circulation.

title: Draft Law of Ukraine “On Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Management”
description:
The draft Law proposes to establish organisational, technical and environmental requirements for producers and economic operators involved in the management of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE), including its collection, storage, transportation, recycling, recovery and disposal.

The draft Law also provides for the introduction of an extended producer responsibility (EPR) system for electrical and electronic equipment (EEE), under which producers are responsible for the entire life cycle of their products, from the manufacture of products through to the collection and treatment of waste generated as a result of their use.

The draft Law proposes to establish a WEEE management system by:

defining the legal, economic and organisational framework for placing electrical and electronic equipment on the market;

defining the methods and procedures for producers to fulfil their obligations;

improving the general characteristics of electrical and electronic equipment to facilitate the dismantling and recovery of WEEE;

applying the waste management hierarchy, including waste prevention, preparation for reuse, recycling and recovery, to WEEE;

establishing requirements for the collection, storage, transportation and treatment, including recycling, of WEEE;

establishing minimum collection and recycling efficiency targets for WEEE;

establishing requirements for producers to take measures to raise public awareness of environmental protection, promote responsible consumption and ensure proper management of WEEE;

introducing an administrative procedure for the registration of producers and extended producer responsibility organisations through the waste management information system;

establishing reporting requirements through the waste management information system, which will also serve as a tool for monitoring and controlling producers’ compliance with their obligations; and

establishing liability for violations of legislation in the field of WEEE management.

The draft Resolution provides for a temporary measure, applicable until 1 January 2027, granting an authorised person of an economic operator the right to inspect a consignment at the place where it is located to verify its compliance with the customs declaration with regard to the quantity of medicines in each batch, to carry out a visual inspection of each batch of medicines, and to submit the relevant photographic materials to the state control authority together with the application for the issuance of a conclusion on the quality of imported medicines. After that date, these provisions will automatically cease to have effect.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Economy and Environment of Ukraine “On Approval of the List of Types of Primary Packaging of Veterinary Medicinal Products Classified as Small-Size Primary Packaging Units”
description:
The draft Order proposes to approve the List of Types of Primary Packaging of Veterinary Medicinal Products Classified as Small-Size Primary Packaging Units.

The draft Order also provides that veterinary medicinal products whose primary packaging labelling does not comply with the requirements of the Order may be placed on the market until 11 April 2031, provided that:

the State registration (re-registration) of the veterinary medicinal products was granted before the date of entry into force of the Order and such registration (re-registration) is valid and indefinite; 
as of the date of entry into force of the Order, an application for State registration (re-registration) is under consideration. In this case, the veterinary medicinal products may be placed on the market after their State registration (re-registration), provided that such registration (re-registration) is indefinite.

The use of veterinary medicinal products placed on the market in accordance with the Order shall be permitted until the end of their shelf life.

title: Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 740 "On Approval of the Procedure for Pharmacovigilance" of 3 June 2026
description:
The Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 740 of 3 June 2026 approves a new Procedure for Pharmacovigilance, developed pursuant to the Law of Ukraine No. 2469-IX of 28 July 2022 “On Medicinal Products” and taking into account recommendations for international harmonisation in the field of pharmacovigilance.

The Procedure establishes:

unified approaches to the establishment and maintenance of pharmacovigilance systems at the state level and by marketing authorisation holders;
requirements for the Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF), which is maintained by the marketing authorisation holder;
minimum requirements for the pharmacovigilance quality system for the state control authority and applicants;
the use of harmonised international terminology, formats and standards in accordance with European practice;
updated requirements for the collection, analysis and monitoring of data on adverse reactions, including through the national pharmacovigilance database;
procedures for the electronic submission of reports on adverse reactions, Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs) and Risk Management Plans (RMPs); 
requirements for post-authorisation safety studies, including the form and content of study protocols and final reports.

The Order also declares invalid the Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 898 of 27 December 2006 “On Approval of the Procedure for Pharmacovigilance”.

title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 213a; Child Restraint Systems--Side Impact Protection; Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 213; Child Restraint Systems, Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 213b; Child Restraint Systems; Incorporation by Reference
description:
This final rule amends the safety standards for child restraint systems (CRSs). The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is amending Federal motor vehicle safety standard (FMVSS) No. 213a, ''Child restraint systems--side impact protection,'' to exempt school bus CRSs from the standard's requirements as long as they meet specified labeling requirements; to delay the compliance date from 30 June 2025 to 5 December 2026; to amend the dummy selection requirements so that the Child Restraint Air Bag Interaction twelve-month-old test dummy (CRABI-12MO) will not be used to test forward-facing CRSs; and to amend positioning procedures for that dummy. The first two of these amendments are in response to petitions from CRS manufacturers. NHTSA is also amending FMVSS No. 213, ''Child restraint systems'' and FMVSS No. 213b, ''Child restraint systems; Mandatory applicability beginning 5 December 2026,'' to exclude school bus CRSs from the requirements to provide attachments for connection to the vehicle's child restraint anchorage system and to change certain labeling requirements to reflect how school bus child restraints are used.

 

The effective date of this final rule is 9 October 2026.    

The revised compliance date for FMVSS No. 213a is 5 December 2026. The compliance date for the updated labeling requirements in FMVSS No. 213 adopted by this final rule is 8 December 2026. The compliance date for the updated labeling requirements in FMVSS No. 213b is 5 December 2026. Optional early compliance with FMVSS Nos. 213, 213a, and 213b is permitted. The incorporation by reference of certain material listed in this rule was approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 24 June 2003 and 5 December 2023.    

If you wish to petition for reconsideration of this rule, your petition must be received by 26 October 2026.

of this rule to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 26 October 2026. title: Telecommunications Relay Service ASCII Format Requirement
description:
In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) amends its rules to eliminate the requirement that Text Telephone (TTY)-based Telecommunications Relay Services (TRS) be capable of communicating in the American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) format. By removing this outdated regulatory mandate, the Commission relieves TRS providers of the obligation to maintain costly and obsolete ASCII-compatible hardware and software systems. Eliminating this requirement will reduce inefficiencies, preserve the integrity of the TRS Fund, and allow providers to redirect resources toward modern relay technologies, all without adversely impacting functional equivalence for consumers who rely on TTY-based TRS.

 

Effective 13 October 2026

title: Partial amendment to the Minimum Requirements for Biological Products
description:
The Minimum Requirements for Biological Products will be amended as follows: 

・Regarding the standard for “Recombinant Adsorbed Hepatitis B Vaccine (Prepared from Yeast)”, “Tests on vector and inserted gene” will be amended to “Tests on inserted gene”.

・Regarding the standard for “Freeze-dried Live Attenuated Rubella Vaccine”, a test by Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) may be used for the Identification Test.

・Regarding the standard for “Freeze-dried Live Attenuated Measles Vaccine”, a test by RT-PCR may be used for the Test for freedom from extraneous viruses and the Identification Test.

・In addition, regarding the standard for “Freeze-dried Live Attenuated Measles-Rubella Combined Vaccine”, a test by RT-PCR may be used for the Confirmation of the labeling.

descriptionPlain: The Minimum Requirements for Biological Products will be amended as follows: ・Regarding the standard for “Recombinant Adsorbed Hepatitis B Vaccine (Prepared from Yeast)”, “Tests on vector and inserted gene” will be amended to “Tests on inserted gene”.・Regarding the standard for “Freeze-dried Live Attenuated Rubella Vaccine”, a test by Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) may be used for the Identification Test.・Regarding the standard for “Freeze-dried Live Attenuated Measles Vaccine”, a test by RT-PCR may be used for the Test for freedom from extraneous viruses and the Identification Test.・In addition, regarding the standard for “Freeze-dried Live Attenuated Measles-Rubella Combined Vaccine”, a test by RT-PCR may be used for the Confirmation of the labeling.

title: The draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine "On Approval of the Requirements for the Composition of Food for Special Medical Purposes"
description:
The draft Order establishes mandatory requirements for the composition and characteristics of food for special medical purposes in line with relevant European Union legislation, including Regulation (EU) No 609/2013 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/128.

The draft Requirements classify food for special medical purposes into three categories: nutritionally complete food with a standard nutrient formulation; nutritionally complete food with a nutrient-adapted formulation specific to a disease, disorder or medical condition; and nutritionally incomplete food with a standard or nutrient-adapted formulation, which is not suitable for use as the sole source of nourishment.

The draft Requirements specify the substances that may be used in the manufacture of food for special medical purposes and establish minimum and maximum levels of vitamins and minerals for products intended for infants and for products intended for population groups other than infants.

They also establish requirements concerning food information, labelling, presentation and advertising.

The draft Order is also being notified under the SPS Agreement.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On approval of the Requirements for the composition of food for total diet replacement for weight control”
description:
The draft Order provides for the approval of mandatory requirements for the composition of food for total diet replacement for weight control.

The draft Requirements stipulate that food for total diet replacement for weight control is intended to replace the entire daily diet.

The draft Requirements specify the substances that may be used in food for total diet replacement for weight control and establish their minimum levels. They also set out requirements concerning the energy value and nutritional content of such products, as well as requirements for food information, labelling, presentation and advertising.

The draft Order is also being notified under the SPS Agreement.

title: Notice of Request To Renew an Approved Information Collection: Mechanically Tenderized Beef Products
description:
In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulations, the Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is announcing its intention to request renewal of the approved information collection regarding the labeling requirements for mechanically tenderized beef products. There are no changes to the information collection. The current approval will expire on 30 June 2027.

 

Submit comments on or before 9 November 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 57125, 8 September 2026:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-08/html/2026-18231.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-08/pdf/2026-18231.pdf

 

This notice, request for comments is identified by Docket Number FSIS-2026-0167. The Docket Folder is available from Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/FSIS-2026-0167/document and provides access to primary documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 9 November 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with FSIS and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

 

Previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/829 are identified by Docket Numbers FSIS-2008-0017, FSIS-2021-0002 and FSIS-2024-0001.

title: United States Standards for Grades of Carcass Beef
description:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is extending the public comment period by 90 days on its Request for Information (RFI) (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/925/Rev.2) concerning revisions to the United States Standards for Grades of Carcass Beef. Stakeholders requested additional time to allow for the completion of research on dentition given that AMS is seeking comments on eliminating the skeletal maturity requirement for carcasses determined by dentition, or documents verifying age, to be under 30 months of age.

 

The comment period for the document originally published on 8 July 2026, (91 FR 42172) is extended 90 days. Comments must be submitted on or before 7 December 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 57125, 8 September 2026:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-08/html/2026-18218.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-08/pdf/2026-18218.pdf

 

This notice; extension of comment period and the notice; request for comments notified as G/TBT/N/USA/925/Rev.2 are identified by Docket Number AMS-LP-25-0485. The Docket Folder is available from Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/AMS-LP-25-0485/document and provides access to primary documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 7 December 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with USDA and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

title: Unleashing Unlicensed Spectrum for Direct-to-Device
description: Proposed rule - The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) issues a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) proposes to expand opportunities for direct-to-device (D2D) communications by permitting certain unlicensed devices to communicate with satellites on a non-interference basis. Building on recent market growth and new industry investment in D2D technologies, the NPRM explores adding satellite allocations in specific unlicensed bands, clarifying that equipment may operate within spacecraft, and establishing a flexible regulatory framework that preserves incumbent operations while enabling continued innovation. The Commission seeks comment on technical, licensing, and policy considerations to support expanded D2D connectivity and ensure coexistence with existing services.

title: National Standard of the P.R.C., Limit of harmful substances in adhesives
description:
This document specifies the product classification, limit requirements for  hazardous substances, inspection rules, and packaging and marking for adhesives, and describes the corresponding test methods.
This document applies to solvent-based, water-based and solvent-free adhesives. This document does not apply to adhesives for national defence and military use, aerospace adhesives, medical adhesives, adhesives for food packaging, or adhesives based on urea-formaldehyde resin, phenolic resin and melamine-formaldehyde resin adhesives for the wood industry.

title: National Standard of the P.R.C, Chinese name for fertilizers—General requirements
description:
This document specifies the basic principles, general requirements, rules for naming common names, and content for labeling of Chinese names for fertilizer.
This document applies to the naming, use, and labeling management of Chinese names for all types of fertilizer products produced (including repackaging of imported products) and sold (including sales of imported products) within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
This document does not apply to the naming, use, and labeling management of Chinese names for specialized fertilizer products that are customized by producers according to contracts for end-users, are not circulated in the market in any form, and are not publicly sold to society.

title: Draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine “Certain Issues Related to the Importation and Quality Control of Medicines”
description:
The draft Resolution has been developed with the aim of regulating the procedures for the importation of medicinal products (excluding active pharmaceutical ingredients) into Ukraine, conducting state quality control of imported medicinal products in a state laboratory or a laboratory authorized by the Ukrainian Pharmaceutical Agency, and carrying out the official batch release of certain biological medicinal products (immunological medicinal products and medicinal products derived from human blood or blood plasma).

The draft Resolution is aimed at implementing the Law of Ukraine No. 2469-IX of 28 July 2022 “On Medicines” and establishing a unified regulatory framework for the relevant procedures applicable to medicinal products imported into Ukraine.

Specifically, the draft Resolution provides for:

Approval of new procedures and criteria:

  1. Procedure for conducting state quality control of medicinal products in a state laboratory or a laboratory authorized by the Ukrainian Pharmaceutical Agency;
  2. Procedure for the official batch release of certain biological medicinal products (immunological medicinal products and medicinal products derived from human blood or blood plasma);
  3. Criteria for establishing an annual programme (plan) for the sampling of medicinal products and the grounds for conducting ad hoc laboratory quality control of medicinal products.

 

Transitional and special provisions for importers:

  1. Establishing a one-year transitional period starting on 1 January 2027 during which importers whose information was not included in the registration dossier as of 1 January 2027 may perform quality control of imported medicinal products without amending the registration dossier, submitting a notification of changes to the licensing information, or obtaining a GMP certificate, under the specified conditions;
  2. Allowing, during the period of martial law and for six months after its termination or cancellation, the import of registered medicinal products in foreign packaging manufactured for the markets of other countries that do not comply with the approved registration dossier, for the purpose of supplying healthcare institutions with medicinal products procured through centralized public procurement, provided that the products are accompanied by a package leaflet (instructions for medical use) approved in Ukraine and a manufacturer's/marketing authorisation holder's guarantee letter confirming that the imported medicinal product is identical to the product registered in Ukraine;
  3. Establishing a procedure for reviewing applications submitted before 1 January 2027 for the issuance of conclusions on the quality of imported medicinal products and on the compliance of medicinal immunobiological products with the requirements of national and international standards, in accordance with the legislation in force prior to the entry into force of the Resolution.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Economy and Environment of  Ukraine  “On Approval of Functional Safety Requirements for the Type-Approval of Agricultural and Forestry Vehicles”
description:
The draft Order proposes to approve requirements for functional safety for the type-approval of agricultural and forestry vehicles, as well as systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, which will establish detailed technical requirements and test procedures.

The Requirements establish specific technical requirements and test procedures concerning functional safety, other than braking systems, for the type-approval of agricultural and forestry vehicles, as well as systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, in accordance with the Technical Regulation on the Type-Approval of Agricultural and Forestry Vehicles, approved by Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 28 of 12 January 2024 (notified in document G/TBT/N/UKR/237/Add.1).

The Requirements have been developed for the implementation of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/208 of 8 December 2014 supplementing Regulation (EU) No. 167/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to vehicle functional safety requirements for the type-approval of agricultural and forestry vehicles.

title: Consumer goods, particularly goods derived from or containing animal-derived materials.
description: The guideline establishes requirements for the implementation of the Halal Product Assurance System (SJPH) and halal certification for consumer goods, particularly goods derived from or containing animal-derived materials. It covers general goods primarily made from animal-derived materials, including leather, fur, hair, horns, and bones, as well as goods made from non-animal or synthetic materials that use animal-derived substances as additives or processing aids during production. The guideline aims to ensure that such goods meet applicable halal requirements and maintain their halal status throughout the production process in accordance with the SJPH criteria and relevant MUI Fatwas.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Information Collection Request; Comment Request; Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles: Heavy-Duty Engine and Vehicle Standards (Renewal)
description:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is planning to submit an information collection request (ICR), Control of Air Pollution from New Motor Vehicles: Heavy-Duty Engine and Vehicle Standards (Renewal) (EPA ICR Number 2621.03, OMB Control Number 2060- 0741) to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act. Before doing so, EPA is soliciting public comments on specific aspects of the proposed information collection as described below. This is a proposed extension of the ICR, which is currently approved through 31 May 2027. This notice allows for 60 days for public comments.

 

Comments must be submitted on or before 3 November 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 56884, 4 September 2026:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-04/html/2026-18168.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-04/pdf/2026-18168.pdf

 

This notice is identified by Docket Number EPA-HQ-OAR-2026-6898. The Docket Folder is available from Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/EPA-HQ-OAR-2026-6898/document and provides access to primary documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 3 November 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with EPA and submitted to the Docket if received within the comment period.

 

Previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/1567 are identified by Docket Number EPA-HQ-OAR-2019-0055.

title: 1,2-Dichloropropane Draft Risk Evaluation Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA); Notice of Availability and Request for Comment
description: Notice of availability and request for comment - The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is announcing the availability of and seeking public comment on a draft risk evaluation under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for 1,2- dichloropropane. The purpose of risk evaluations under TSCA is to determine whether a chemical substance presents an unreasonable risk of injury to health or the environment under the conditions of use (COUs), including unreasonable risk to potentially exposed or susceptible subpopulations identified as relevant to the risk evaluation by EPA, and without consideration of costs or non-risk factors. EPA is seeking comment on the draft risk evaluation for 1,2-dichloropropane.

title: Regulations Amending the Passenger Automobile and Light Truck Greenhouse Gas Regulations
description:
The purpose of the Passenger Automobile and Light Truck Greenhouse Gas Emission Regulations is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from passenger automobiles and light trucks.

On December 20, 2023, amendments to the Passenger Automobile and Light Truck Greenhouse Gas Emission Regulations introduced new requirements for manufacturers and importers to ensure that their fleet of new light-duty vehicles offered for sale in Canada would meet specified annual targets of zero emission vehicles, known as the Electric Vehicle Availability Standard.

The purpose of the proposed Regulations Amending the Passenger Automobile and Light Truck Greenhouse Gas Emission Regulations is to repeal the Electric Vehicle Availability Standard, in line with commitments announced by the Prime Minister of Canada in February 2026. The proposed Regulations Amending the Passenger Automobile and Light Truck Greenhouse Gas Emission Regulations will also make changes to maintain the functioning of the Passenger Automobile and Light Truck Greenhouse Gas Emission Regulations following the repeal of greenhouse gas emission regulations in the United States.

The Passenger Automobile and Light Truck Greenhouse Gas Emission Regulations were previously notified to the WTO in G/TBT/N/CAN/688 and G/TBT/N/CAN/688/Add.1.

title:
Draft Unsafe Goods (Consumer Sand Products) Notice 2026 (6 pages, in English), https://www.mbie.govt.nz/have-your-say/consultation-on-draft-unsafe-goods-consumer-sand-products-notice-2026.

The draft notice would be made under the Fair Trading Act 1986 and would declare certain toys containing sand and decorative, craft or artistic goods containing accessible sand to be unsafe goods unless prescribed asbestos testing requirements have been met. The notice incorporates by reference:

  • ISO 22262-2:2026, Air quality — Bulk materials — Part 2: Quantitative determination of asbestos by gravimetric and microscopical methods (50 pages, in English).
description:
The proposed Unsafe Goods (Consumer Sand Products Containing Asbestos) Notice 2026 would prohibit the supply of specified consumer sand products unless suppliers hold evidence demonstrating that the products do not contain asbestos.

The notice would apply to:

  • goods that are a toy that is, include, or contain sand; and
  • goods that are a decorative, craft or artistic good that are sand or that include or contain accessible sand.

The notice would not apply to sand produced by natural geological processes that is intended to fill sand pits, playgrounds, or other recreational areas.

To demonstrate compliance, suppliers would be required to:

  • obtain negative asbestos test results for at least three samples of a product, which includes:
  • obtaining testing using Scanning Electron Microscopy with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) or Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) using the applicable procedures specified in ISO 22262-2:2026;
  • ensuring testing is conducted by a laboratory accredited to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 by an accreditation body that is a signatory to the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation Mutual Recognition Arrangement (ILAC MRA);
  • ensure those samples were tested within the 12 months preceding importation (for imported goods) or manufacture (for domestically manufactured goods); and
  • have a test certificate, test report, test result, or other document recording the results of the testing and meets specified requirements (such as indicating that no asbestos was detected in the samples tested).

The measure is intended as an interim requirement pending development of longer-term product safety regulation addressing asbestos contamination in consumer sand products.
productsFreeText:
Consumer products containing sand, including:

  • Toys containing sand (whether sand is accessible or sealed within the toy), excluding natural sand intended for sand pits.
  • Decorative, craft and artistic goods containing accessible sand.

  • 97.200.50 Toys
  • 97.195 Works of art and handicrafts
  • 97.190 Equipment for children

objectivesFreeText: Since November 2025, New Zealand suppliers have undertaken 23 recalls of consumer sand products following the detection of asbestos contamination, affecting approximately 46,000 units. Research has demonstrated that asbestos fibres may become airborne during normal use of some sand products, creating a risk of inhalation and associated adverse health effects. The proposed measure seeks to prevent the supply of asbestos-contaminated consumer sand products in New Zealand. The use of an internationally recognised testing method and laboratory accreditation requirements intend to provide a consistent and reliable basis for demonstrating compliance.

title: Notice of Availability and Request for Comment: Revision to the Voluntary Standard for Products Containing Button Cell or Coin Batteries
description:
The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's (Commission or CPSC) mandatory rule, Safety Standard for Button Cell or Coin Batteries and Consumer Products Containing Such Products, incorporates by reference UL 4200A, Standard for Safety for Products Incorporating Button Batteries or Coin Cell Batteries. UL notified the Commission that it has revised this incorporated voluntary standard. CPSC seeks comment on whether the revision improves the safety of button cell or coin batteries and consumer products containing such products.

 

Comments must be received by 17 September 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 56604; 3 September 2026:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-03/html/2026-18103.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-03/pdf/2026-18103.pdf

 

This notice of availability, request for comment is identified by Docket Number CPSC-2023-0004. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/CPSC-2023-0004/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders by 4pm Eastern Time on 17 September 2026 will be shared with CPSC and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

 

Previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/1964 are identified by Docket Numbers CPSC-2023-0004 and CPSC-2024-0004.

description: The notified draft Royal Decree consists of a preamble, a single article approving the Regulation, six additional provisions, seven transitional provisions, one repealing provision and seven final provisions. The regulatory structure of the Regulation comprises 30 articles containing general provisions and 13 supplementary technical instructions that establish specific technical requirements.The purpose of this Royal Decree is to update the technical regulations in order to better adapt them to current needs, possibilities and technical solutions relating to gas fuel installations, taking into account technological developments and the experience gained through the application of the current Regulation.The draft Royal Decree consists of:• Single article. Approval of the Regulation.G/TBT/N/ESP/62- 2 - • First additional provision. Technical guide.• Second additional provision. Insurance cover or other equivalent guarantee taken out in another State.• Third additional provision. Acceptance of documents from other member States for the purposes of demonstrating compliance with requirements.• Fourth additional provision. Equivalence of requirements.• Fifth additional provision. Model declaration of responsibility.• Sixth additional provision. Obligations concerning information and complaints.• First transitional provision. Inspection bodies authorized prior to the entry into force of this Royal Decree.• Second transitional provision. Administrative regularization of installations.• Third transitional provision. Periodic reviews and inspections of existing installations.• Fourth transitional provision. Installations under construction on the date of entry into force of the Regulation.• Fifth transitional provision. Previously authorized gas installation companies.• Sixth transitional provision. Gas appliances.• Seventh transitional provision. Installations affected by the fourth final provision that are under construction upon the entry into force of this Royal Decree.• Single repealing provision. Repeal of legislation.• First final provision. Amendment to Royal Decree No. 552/2019 of 27 September approving the Regulation on safety for refrigerating installations and its supplementary technical instructions.• Second final provision. Amendment to the Regulation on pressure equipment and its supplementary technical instruction ITC EP-6 "Transportable pressure vessels", approved by Royal Decree No. 809/2021 of 21 September.• Third final provision. Amendment to Royal Decree No. 337/2014 of 9 May approving the Regulation on technical conditions and safety guarantees for high-voltage electrical installations and its supplementary technical instructions ITC-RAT 01 to 23.• Fourth final provision. Amendment to Royal Decree No. 656/2017 of 23 June approving the Regulation on the storage of chemical products and its supplementary technical instructions MIE APQ 0 to 10.• Fifth final provision. Competence.• Sixth final provision. Technical update.• Seventh final provision. Entry into force.

title: DEAS 1133: 2023, Firefighting vehicle — Specification, First Edition
description:
Kenya would like to inform WTO Members that the draft East African Standard; DEAS 1133: 2023, Firefighting vehicle — Specification, First Edition

 notified in, G/TBT/N/BDI/384, G/TBT/N/KEN/1464, G/TBT/N/RWA/896, G/TBT/N/TZA/998, G/TBT/N/UGA/1802 was adopted and published by Kenya as KS EAS 1133:2026 Kenya Standard—Firefighting vehicle— Specification, First Edition on 7th August 2026 via Kenya Gazette, No. 12185 dated 7th August 2026.

A copy of the document can be obtained via the following link at a basic fee: https://webstore.kebs.go.ke

title: Draft Notification of the Ministry of Public Health Re: Refurbished Medical Device B.E. .…
description:
The Minister of Public Health hereby issues the draft notification on refurbished medical devices as follows:

• Definitions of ‘Refurbished medical device’, ‘Product owner’ and ‘Authorized representative’

• Refurbished medical devices shall be refurbished by the product owner or its authorized representative.

• Refurbished medical devices specified in the annex to the notification shall comply with IEC 63077, applicable quality management system requirements, including ISO 13485 (within the scope of refurbishment), and labeling requirements.
productsFreeText: Medical Devices

objectives.name: Prevention of deceptive practices and consumer protection (TBT)

objectivesFreeText: To regulate refurbished medical devices appropriately and effectively to ensure quality and consumer protection.

title: Temporary Exemption From Motor Vehicle Safety and Bumper Standards
description:
In response to a request from the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (Auto Innovators), the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is announcing a 30-day extension of the public comment period for the interim final rule (IFR) published on 31 July 2026 (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/1436/Add.1) amending NHTSA's general exemption regulations to remove language limiting the application of temporary exemptions from the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS) and the bumper standard to motor vehicles manufactured on and after the effective date of an exemption, and to align the regulations with the Administrator's statutory discretion to determine the vehicle population covered by a temporary exemption. The notice also removed the requirement that applications for exemption be submitted in three copies and specified an electronic means for submission. The comment period for the notice was originally scheduled to end on 31 August 2026. It will now end on 30 September 2026.

 

The comment period for the IFR published on 31 July 2026 at 91 FR 48307, is extended. Comments should be received on or before 30 September 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 55793, 31 August 2026; Title 49 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 555:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-31/html/2026-17742.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-31/pdf/2026-17742.pdf

 

This extension of comment period and the interim final rule notified as G/TBT/N/USA/1436/Add.1 are identified by Docket Number NHTSA-2026-1585. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/NHTSA-2026-1585/document and provides access to primary documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 30 September 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with NHTSA and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

title: Resetting NHTSA's Fuel Economy Program: Commercial Medium- and Heavy-Duty On-Highway Vehicles and Work Trucks
description: Interpretive rule - The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is issuing this interpretive rule regarding the scope of its authority to set fuel economy standards for commercial medium- and heavy-duty on-highway vehicles and work trucks. This rule describes NHTSA's authority to set vehicle standards, which does not include the authority to set separate standards for engines. NHTSA will review its existing standards applicable to commercial medium- and heavy-duty on-highway vehicles and work trucks for consistency with this interpretation in a separate rulemaking. Pending the rulemaking process, NHTSA will exercise its enforcement authority with regard to affected standards in accordance with the interpretation set forth in this rule.
